mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the pattern reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters, or the pattern fails during periods of strong monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month indicates a sharp decline in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the pattern fails during supply-chain normalization.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening in monetary and price pressures, which increases discount rates and reduces real earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the pattern reverses when GDP growth is accelerating.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 5% signals elevated precautionary savings behavior by households, which reduces current consumption and investment demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect is absent during periods of fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) where PAYEMS grows while UNRATE falls below 4% indicates a labor market overheating, which raises wage growth and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the pattern reverses during periods of falling inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which reduces construction-related corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears during periods of strong mortgage rate declines.
